title: He Sawed The Legs Off A Table In 1956. It Became IKEA's Entire Business Model.
description:
Educational purposes only. Not financial advice.

In 1956, IKEA designer Gillis Lundgren couldn't fit a table into his Volvo, so he removed the legs and packed it flat. That accident became IKEA's core business model: ship furniture unassembled, let the customer build it, and fit far more product into every truck and container. It's how a Swedish catalog company grew into one of the largest furniture retailers in the world.
